x: Commentary on Sūrat “Iqraʾ”. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
On the interpretation of the saying of Him whose praise is majestic and whose names are sanctified:

Recite in the name of your Lord who created (1) Created man from a clinging clot (2) Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous (3) Who taught by the pen (4) Taught man that which he knew not (5) No! Indeed, man transgresses (6) Because he sees himself self-sufficient (7) Indeed, to your Lord is the return (8)
Recite in the name of your Lord
, He, majestic is His praise, means Muḥammad.
Recite, Muḥammad, with the mention of your Lord who created. Then He made clear who it was that created, so He said:
Created man from a clinging clot
He means: from blood. And He said:

, the intended meaning being: from an ʿalaqah (a clot), for He had the plural in mind, as one says shajarah and shajar (tree, trees), qaṣabah and qaṣab (reed, reeds); so likewise ʿalaqah and ʿalaq. He said
although “man” is a singular expression, because it is plural in meaning even if singular in expression; hence it was said:
Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous
and your Lord is the most Generous (3) Who taught by the pen

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Recite in the name of your Lord who created
. He said: The pen is a great favour from God; were it not for it, livelihood would not stand firm nor be sound
. It has been said that this is the first sūrah revealed in the Qurʾān to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Aḥmad b. ʿUthmān al-Baṣrī told me, he said: Wahb b. Jarīr told us, he said: my father told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Nuʿmān b. Rāshid say, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah, that she said: The first thing with which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was begun of the revelation was the true dream, which would come like the breaking of dawn. Then solitude was made beloved to him, and he would be in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, devoting himself to worship there for a number of nights before returning to his family; then he would return to his family and take provisions for the like of it, until the truth came upon him suddenly. [The angel] came to him and said: “Muḥammad, you are the Messenger of God.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I dropped on my knees while standing, then I returned, my shoulder-muscles
trembling, and I went in to Khadījah and said: ‘Wrap me up, wrap me up!’ until the fright left me. Then he came to me and said: ‘Muḥammad
, you are the Messenger of God.’” He said: “I had in fact resolved to throw myself down from the peak of a mountain, [and he appeared to me]
just when I had resolved to do so, and said: ‘Muḥammad, I am Gabriel and you are the Messenger of God.’ Then he said:
. I said: ‘What shall I recite?’” He said: (“He took me and squeezed me three times, until it took its toll of me, then said:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created

. So I recited. Then I came to Khadījah and said: ‘I feared for myself.’ And I told her my story. She said: ‘Rejoice! By God, God will never disgrace you. By God, you maintain the ties of kinship, you speak the truth, you fulfil trusts, you bear the burdens of others, you honour the guest, and you help against the misfortunes of [befalling] the right.’ Then she took me to Waraqah b. Nawfal b. Asad and said: ‘Listen to your cousin.’

c: He questioned me and I told him
m: my story. He said: ‘This is the Nāmūs that was sent down to Moses. Would that I were a young man in it

; would that I were alive when your people drive you out.’ I said: ‘Will they drive me out?’ He said: ‘Yes. No man has ever come with what you have come with without being met with hostility; and if your day reaches me, I will support you with strong support.’ Then the first thing revealed to me of the Qurʾān after “Iqraʾ” was:

Nūn. By the pen and what they inscribe (1) You are not, by the favour of your Lord, a madman (2) And indeed, for you is a reward unending (3) And indeed, you are of a great moral character (4) So you will see, and they will see
O you who covers himself [with a garment] (1) Arise and warn
By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Yūnus informed me, from Ibn Shihāb, he said: ʿUrwah told me that ʿĀʾishah informed him
m: —and he mentioned the like of it, except that he did not say: “Then the first thing revealed to me of the Qurʾān…”—the discourse to its end

c: Ibn Abī l-Shawārib told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid told us, he said: Sulaymān al-Shaybānī told us, he said: ʿAbdallāh b. Shaddād told us, he said:
m: Gabriel came to Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Muḥammad, recite.” He said: “What shall I recite?” He said: So he embraced him tightly, then said: “Muḥammad, recite.” He said: “What shall I recite?” He said:
In the name of your Lord who created
Taught man that which he knew not

. He said: Then he came to Khadījah and said: (“Khadījah, I think nothing but that something has befallen me.” She said: “Never! By God, your Lord would not do that to you, and you have never committed an indecency.” He said: So Khadījah went to Waraqah and told him the report. He said: “If you are truthful, then your husband is a prophet, and he will certainly meet hardship from his community; and if I live to see him, I will surely believe in him.” He said: Then Gabriel was slow in coming to him, and Khadījah said to him: “I see nothing but that your Lord has detested you.” So God revealed:
“By the morning brightness (1) And [by] the night when it covers with darkness
Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you]” [al-Ḍuḥā: 1–3] (1).

c: Ibrāhīm b. Saʿīd al-Jawharī told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah—Ibrāhīm
m: said: Sufyān said: Ibn Isḥāq memorised it for us—that the first thing revealed of the Qurʾān was:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created

c: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Bishr b. al-Ḥakam al-Naysābūrī told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Muḥammad b.
m: Isḥāq, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀʾishah: The first sūrah revealed of the Qurʾān was:
Recite in the name of your Lord

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, from ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr, he said: The first sūrah revealed to Muḥammad, the Messenger of God, was:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created
. He said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī told us, he said:

c: Shuʿbah told us, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, he said: I heard ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr say—and he mentioned the like of it.

c: Khallād b. Aslam told us, he said: al-Naḍr b. Shumayl informed us, he said: Qurrah told us, he said: Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī informed us, he said:
m: We were in the congregational mosque, and our reciter was Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī—it is as if I am looking at him between two white cloaks. Abū Rajāʾ said: From him I took this sūrah:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created
; and it was the first sūrah revealed to Muḥammad.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq told me, from one of his companions, from ʿAṭāʾ b.
m: Yasār, he said: The first sūrah revealed of the Qurʾān was:
Recite in the name of your Lord

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Yaḥyā and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Mahdī told us, both said: Sufyān told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, he said:
m: The first thing revealed of the Qurʾān was:
Recite in the name of your Lord

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAmr b.
m: Dīnār, he said: I heard ʿUbayd b. ʿUmayr say: The first thing revealed of the Qurʾān was:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created

. He said: Wakīʿ told us, from Qurrah b. Khālid, from Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī, he said: I can see Abū Mūsā now as he recites the Qurʾān in the mosque of Basra, wearing two white cloaks; and I took from him:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created
, and it is the first sūrah revealed to Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace
. He said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, he said: The first sūrah revealed was:
Recite in the name of your Lord who created

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid,

x: Taught man that which he knew not
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: He taught man writing with the pen, which he did not know, along with other things besides that which He taught him and which he did not know.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on the saying of God:
Taught man that which he knew not
. He said: He taught man writing with the pen.

x: . The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: It is not thus that man should be: that his Lord should favour him by fashioning his creation well, teaching him what he did not know, and bestowing on him blessings that have no equal, and then he should disbelieve in his Lord who did that to him, and transgress against Him because he sees himself self-sufficient.
Indeed, man transgresses (6) Because he sees himself self-sufficient
. He says: Indeed, man oversteps his bounds and is arrogant toward his Lord and so disbelieves in Him, because he sees himself as having become self-sufficient. It is said

because the verb “raʾā” requires a subject and an object [predicate]; and so the Arabs do with every verb that requires a subject and an object, when the speaker applies it to himself, referring to himself by a pronoun [he uses an indirect reference], saying: “When do you see yourself going out?” and “When do you reckon yourself travelling?” But when the verb requires only a single object in the accusative, they put “nafsah” (himself) in the place of the pronoun, so they say: “You killed yourself (qatalta nafsaka),” and do not say: “You killed you (qataltaka),” nor “he killed him (qatalahu)”
Indeed, to your Lord is the return
. He says: Indeed, to your Lord, Muḥammad, is his return, and he will taste of His painful punishment what he has no power to withstand.
On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays? (10)

. It is mentioned that this verse and those after it were revealed about Abū Jahl b. Hishām, because he said, according to what has reached us: “If I see Muḥammad praying, I will tread on his neck.” And, as is mentioned, he had forbidden the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray; so God said to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you seen, Muḥammad, Abū Jahl, who forbids you to pray at the Maqām, while he turns away from the truth, denying it? Majestic is His praise, He makes His Prophet and the believers marvel at the ignorance of Abū Jahl and his audacity toward his Lord in forbidding Muḥammad to pray to his Lord, while, despite His favours to him, he denies Him.
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on the saying of God:
Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays?
. He said: Abū Jahl, who forbids Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he prays

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays?
: It was revealed about the enemy of God, Abū Jahl; that is because he said: “If I see Muḥammad praying, I will tread on his neck.” So God revealed what you hear.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays?
. He said: Abū Jahl said: “If I see Muḥammad praying, I will tread on his neck.” He said: And it used to be said: Every community has a Pharaoh, and the Pharaoh of this community is Abū Jahl

c: Isḥāq b. Shāhīn al-Wāsiṭī told us, he said: Khālid b. ʿAbdallāh told us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying, and Abū Jahl came to him and forbade him to pray, so God revealed:
Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays?

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
Have you seen if he is upon guidance (11) Or enjoins righteousness? (12)
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Have you seen, if Muḥammad were
, meaning: upon uprightness and rectitude in his prayer to his Lord,
: or if this Muḥammad—whom the one who forbids prayer is forbidding—were to enjoin fear of God and dread of His punishment?
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: Have you seen if he is upon guidance (11) Or enjoins righteousness?
. He said: Muḥammad was upon guidance and enjoined righteousness

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
Have you seen if he denies and turns away? (13)
. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Have you seen, if Abū Jahl denies the truth with which Muḥammad was sent
. He says: [and turns his back on it and does not believe it]
The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Have you seen if he denies and turns away?

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:

Does he not know that God sees? (14) No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock (15) A lying, sinning forelock (16) Then let him call his associates (17) We will call the guards of Hell (18) No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to God] (19)

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Does Abū Jahl not know, when he forbids Muḥammad from worshipping his Lord and praying to Him, that God sees him, so that he should fear His might and His punishment? It was said:
Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays? (10) Have you seen if he is upon guidance

. So “Have you seen” was repeated three times as a substitution. And the meaning is: Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays—while he himself denies and turns away from his Lord—does he not know that God sees him?
. He says: It is not as he says
: that he will tread on the neck of Muḥammad. He says: He has no power over that, nor will he reach him.
. He says: If Abū Jahl does not desist from [harming] Muḥammad,
We will surely seize [him] by the forelock
. He says: We will surely take hold of the front of his head and subdue
him and humble him. One says of it: “I seized (safaʿtu) his hand,” when you take hold of his hand. It is also said that
We will surely seize by the forelock

means: We will surely blacken his face; the mention of the forelock sufficed for the whole face, since the forelock is at the front of the face. It is also said that the meaning is: We will surely take him by his forelock to the Fire, as it is said (1):
And they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet
is in the genitive, as a repetition in apposition to the first “forelock.” He described the forelock as lying and sinning, the meaning being [that this is said] of its owner.
Then let him call his associates

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Then let Abū Jahl call the people of his assembly and his supporters from his clan and his people. The nādī is the assembly. It was said so, according to what has reached us, because when Abū Jahl forbade the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray at the Maqām, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked him and was harsh with him, and Abū Jahl said: “For what does Muḥammad threaten me, when I have the largest assembly (nādiyan) of anyone in the valley?” So God, majestic is His praise, said:
If he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock

; let him then call his assembly, for if he calls his assembly, We will call the guards of Hell. Reports have come, and the people of interpretation have spoken, in the like of what we have said about this.
Mention of the traditions reported on that:

c: Ibn Wakīʿ told us, he said: Abū Khālid al-Aḥmar told us; and Abū Kurayb told us, he said: al-Ḥakam b. Jumayʿ told us, he said: ʿAlī b. Mushir told us,
m: both from Dāwūd b. Abī Hind, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying at the Maqām, and Abū Jahl b. Hishām passed by him and said: “Muḥammad, did I not forbid you from this?” and threatened him; so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was harsh with him and rebuked him, and [Abū Jahl] said: “Muḥammad, with what do you threaten me? By God, I have the largest assembly in this valley.” So God revealed:
Then let him call his associates (17) We will call the guards of Hell
. Ibn ʿAbbās said: Had he called his assembly, the guards of punishment would have seized him that very hour

c: Isḥāq b. Shāhīn told me, he said: Khālid b. ʿAbdallāh told us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying, and Abū Jahl came to him and forbade him to pray, so God revealed:
Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays?

. He said: “He knows that I have the largest assembly in this valley.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and said something—Dāwūd said: and I did not memorise it—so God revealed:
Then let him call his associates (17) We will call the guards of Hell
. Ibn ʿAbbās said: By God, had he done so, the angels would have seized him from his place

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said:
m: told us, from his father, he said: Nuʿaym b. Abī Hind told us, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Abū Hurayrah, he said: Abū Jahl said: “Does Muḥammad rub his face in the dust among you?” It was said: “Yes.” He said: “By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, if I see him praying like that, I will tread on his neck, or
rub his face in the dust.” He said: So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying, to tread on his neck. He said: Then what startled them

about him was that he was retreating on his heels and shielding himself with his hands. He said: It was said to him: “What is the matter with you?” He said: “Between me and him is a trench of fire, and terror, and wings.” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Had he come near, the angels would have snatched him limb by limb.” He said: And God revealed—I do not know whether this is in the report of Abū Hurayrah or not—:

No! Indeed, man transgresses (6) Because he sees himself self-sufficient (7) Indeed, to your Lord is the return (8) Have you seen the one who forbids (9) A servant when he prays? (10) Have you seen if he is upon guidance (11) Or enjoins righteousness? (12) Have you seen if he denies and turns away?

Does he not know that God sees? (14) No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock (15) A lying, sinning forelock (16) Then let him call his associates (5) (17) We will call the guards of Hell
No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to God]

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ told us, he said: Yūnus b. Abī Isḥāq informed us, from al-Walīd b.
m: al-ʿAyzār, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Abū Jahl said: “If Muḥammad returns to praying at the Maqām, I will kill him.” So God revealed:
Recite in the name of your Lord
We will surely seize [him] by the forelock (15) A lying, sinning forelock (16) Then let him call his associates (17) We will call the guards of Hell

. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying, and it was said to him: “What prevents you?” He said: “What lies between me and him has become black with battalions.” Ibn ʿAbbās said: By God, had he moved, the angels would have seized him while the people were looking at him

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Zakariyyā b. ʿAdī told us, he said: ʿUbaydallāh b. ʿAmr told us, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: Abū Jahl said:
m: praying at the Kaʿbah, I will come to him until I tread on his neck.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Had he done so, the angels would have seized him in plain sight”
. And the people of interpretation have spoken in accordance with what we said about the meaning of “al-nādī.”

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: Then let him call his associates
. He says: let him call his supporter

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
We will call the guards of Hell

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Abū Sinān, from ʿAbdallāh b.
m: Abī l-Hudhayl: The zabāniyah have their feet on the earth and their heads in the heaven

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah,
m: We will call the guards of Hell
: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Had Abū Jahl done so, the zabāniyah, the angels, would have seized him in plain sight.”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: We will call the guards of Hell

c: I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, on His saying:

x: . The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: The matter is not as Abū Jahl says, when he forbids Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to worship his Lord and pray to Him;
. Majestic is His praise, He says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not obey Abū Jahl in what he commands you, namely to abandon prayer to your Lord;
to Him, by endearing yourself to Him through obedience to Him; for Abū Jahl will not be able to harm you, and We shall protect you from him.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to God]
: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed about Abū Jahl, who said: “If I see Muḥammad praying, I will tread on
No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near [to God]

. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when what Abū Jahl had said reached him: “Had he done so, the zabāniyah would have snatched him.” End of Sūrat “Iqraʾ bi-smi Rabbika”; and praise belongs to God alone.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/369) to the author, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 369 إلى المصنف وعبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Al-bawadir is the plural of badirah, the muscle between the shoulder and neck. See Taj al-ʿArus, root b-d-r.
notes.ar: البوادر جمع بادرة، وهى اللحمة التي بين المنكب والعنق. التاج (ب د ر).

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “I am Gabriel, and …” after it.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "أنا جبريل و".

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “fa-tamaththala ilayya”; T2 reads “fa-ʿada li”; T3 reads “fa-ʿada ilayya.”
notes.ar: في م: "فتمثل إليّ"، وفى ت 2: "فعدا لى"، وفى ت 3: "فعاد إلى".

notes.en: The pronoun in “in it” refers to prophethood. “I wish I had been young when it appeared, so I could give my utmost in supporting and protecting it.” See al-Nihaya (1/250).
notes.ar: الضمير في "فيها " للنبوة، لى: يا ليتنى كنت شابًّا عند ظهورها حتى أبالغ في نصرتها وحمايتها. النهاية 1/ 250.

notes.en: The manuscripts omit it; it is restored from the author’s History.
notes.ar: سقط من النسخ، والمثبت من تاريخ المصنف.

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History (2/298). ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 9719), Ahmad (6/153, 223, 232, al-Maymaniyya edition), al-Bukhari (nos. 3, 4956), Muslim (160/253–254), al-Tirmidhi (no. 3632), and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 5) transmitted a similar report through several chains from al-Zuhri. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/368) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 2/ 298. وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في المصنف (9719)، وأحمد 6/ 153، 223، 232) (الميمنية)، والبخارى (3، 4956)، ومسلم (160/ 253، 254)، والترمذى (3632)، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 5 من طرق عن الزهرى به بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 68 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن الأنبارى في المصاحف وابن مردويه.

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History (1/299). Muslim (160/252) and al-Bayhaqi (9/5–6) transmitted it through Ibn Wahb; Ahmad (6/153, al-Maymaniyya edition) and al-Bukhari (no. 4953) transmitted it through Yunus.
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه. 1/ 299. وأخرجه مسلم (160/ 252)، والبيهقي 9/ 5، 6 من طريق ابن وهب به، وأخرجه أحمد 6/ 153 (الميمنية)، والبخارى (4953)، من طريق يونس به.

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History (1/299). Ibn Abi Shayba (14/292) transmitted a similar report through Abu Ishaq Sulayman al-Shaybani. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/368) to Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف في تاريخه 1/ 299. وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 14/ 292 من طريق أبي إسحاق سليمان الشيباني به بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 368 إلى أبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.en: Al-Bayhaqi (9/6; al-Dalaʾil 2/155), al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (pp. 5–6), and al-Baghawi in his Tafsir (8/478) transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Bishr ibn al-Hakam. Al-Hakim (2/220, 529) transmitted it through Sufyan. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/368) to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي 9/ 6، وفى الدلائل، 2/ 155، والواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 5، 6، والبغوى في تفسيره 8/ 478 من طريق عبد الرحمن بن بشر بن الحكم به، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 220، 529 من طريق سفيان به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 368 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba (14/88) transmitted it through Shuʿba, and ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/385) through ʿAmr ibn Dinar.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 14/ 88 من طريق شعبة به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 385 من طريق عمرو بن دينار به.

notes.en: Abu ʿUbayd transmitted it in Fadaʾil al-Qurʾan (p. 220) from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi with this chain. Ibn Abi Shayba (10/541; 14/88) transmitted it through Sufyan. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/368) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو عبيد في الفضائل ص 220 عن عبد الرحمن بن مهدي به. مهدي به. وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 10/ 541، 14/ 88 من طريق سفيان به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 368 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it (10/541; 14/88) from Wakiʿ with this chain.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 10/ 541، 14/ 88 عن وكيع به.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it (10/542; 14/88), and Abu Nuʿaym in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (1/257), through Wakiʿ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 10/ 542، 14/ 88، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 1/ 257 من طريق وكيع به، وأخرجه =

notes.en: Continuation: Yunus ibn Bukayr in his additions to Ibn Ishaq’s Sirah (p. 103), Ibn al-Durays in Fadaʾil al-Qurʾan (no. 24), al-Hakim (2/220), and Abu Nuʿaym in Hilyat al-Awliyaʾ (1/256) transmitted it through Qurra. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/368) to Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: = يونس بن بكير في زياداته على سيرة ابن إسحاق ص 103 وابن الضريس في الفضائل (24)، والحاكم 2/ 220، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 1/ 256 من طريق قرة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 368 إلى ابن الأنبارى في المصاحف والطبراني وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “qataltuhu” (“I killed him”).
notes.ar: في م: "قتلته".

notes.en: Tafsir Mujahid, p. 739. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/370) to al-Firyabi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 739، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 370 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzaq transmitted it in his Tafsir (2/384) from Maʿmar with this chain. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/370) to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 384 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 370 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ahmad (5/167, no. 3044), al-Hakim (2/487–488), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil (2/192) transmitted it through Dawud. Al-Tabarani (no. 11950) transmitted it through ʿIkrima. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/369) to Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 5/ 167 (3044)، والحاكم 2/ 487، 488، والبيهقى في الدلائل 2/ 192 من طريق داود به، وأخرجه الطبراني (11950) من طريق عكرمة به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 369 إلى ابن المنذر وأبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.en: The beginning was cited on the preceding page; this wording is not found in ʿAbd al-Razzaq.
notes.ar: تقدم أوله في الصفحة السابقة، ولم يرد هذا اللفظ عند عبد الرزاق.

notes.en: Manuscripts S, T1, T2, and T3 read: “then he turned away from him and did not believe in him.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2 ت 3: "فأدبر عنه ولم يصدق به".

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “qala” (“he said”).
notes.ar: في م: "قال".

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “fa-l-nadmanahu.”
notes.ar: في م: "فلنضمنه".

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba (14/298), Ahmad (4/164, no. 2321), al-Tirmidhi (no. 3349), and al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11684) transmitted it through Abu Khalid. Ibn Mardawayh—as cited in al-Zaylaʿi’s takhrij of al-Kashshaf (4/248)—transmitted it through ʿAli ibn Mushir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 14/ 298، وأحمد 4/ 164 (2321)، والترمذى (3349)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11684) من طريق أبي خالد به. وأخرجه ابن مردويه - كما في تخريج الكشاف للزيلعي 4/ 248 - من طريق على بن مسهر به.

notes.en: The source references were given earlier on p. 534.
notes.ar: تقدم تخريجه في ص 534.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Ibn Thawr”; the adopted form follows the sources documenting the report.
notes.ar: في النسخ: "ابن ثور" والمثبت من مصادر التخريج.

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “wa” (“and”).
notes.ar: في م: "و".

notes.en: Manuscript M reads “fa-jaʾahu.” Both forms have the same meaning. See Taj al-ʿArus, root f-j-ʾ.
notes.ar: في م: "فجأه". وكلاهما بمعنى. ينظر تاج العروس (ف ج أ).

notes.en: Manuscript M adds “he calls his people” after it.
notes.ar: بعده في م: "يدعو قومه".

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/461) from the author. Muslim (2797/28), al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11683), Ibn Abi Hatim—as cited in Ibn Kathir’s Tafsir—and al-Baghawi in his Tafsir (8/479) transmitted it through Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla. Ahmad (14/425, no. 8831), Muslim (2797/28), Ibn Hibban (no. 6571), Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil (no. 158), al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil (2/198), and al-Baghawi in his Tafsir (8/479) transmitted it through Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 461 عن المصنف، وأخرجه مسلم (2797/ 28)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11683)، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير - والبغوى في تفسيره 8/ 479 من طريق محمد بن عبد الأعلى به، وأخرجه أحمد 14/ 425 (8831)، ومسلم (2797/ 28)، وابن حبان (6571)، وأبو نعيم في الدلائل (158)، والبيهقى في الدلائل 2/ 198، والبغوى في تفسيره 8/ 479 من طريق معتمر بن سليمان به.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/461) from the author. Al-Tabarani (no. 12693; al-Awsat, no. 8398) transmitted it through Yunus. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/369) to Abu Nuʿaym in al-Dalaʾil.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 461 عن المصنف، وأخرجه الطبراني (12693)، وفى الأوسط (8398) من طريق يونس به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 369 إلى أبي نعيم في الدلائل.

notes.en: This is how it appears in the manuscripts; S, M, T1, and T add “peace and blessings be upon him” after it. Abu Jahl would not say that.
notes.ar: كذا في النسخ، وبعده في ص، م، ت 1، ت: " صلى الله عليه وسلم". وأبو جهل لا يقوله.

notes.en: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir (8/460) from the author. Al-Bazzar (no. 2189, Kashf) and Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir—as cited in al-Fath (8/724)—transmitted it through Zakariyya ibn ʿAdi. Abu Yaʿla (no. 2604) and al-Baghawi in Muntakhab al-Musnad—as cited in al-Fath (8/724)—transmitted it through ʿUbaydullah ibn ʿAmr. ʿAbd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir (2/384)—and through him Ahmad (5/437, no. 3483)—al-Bukhari (no. 4958), al-Tirmidhi (no. 3348), al-Nasaʾi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (no. 11685), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dalaʾil (2/191–192) transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Karim.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 8/ 460 عن المصنف، وأخرجه البزار (2189 - كشف)، وابن مردويه في تفسيره - كما في الفتح 8/ 724 - من طريق زكريا بن عدى به. وأخرجه أبو يعلى (2604)، والبغوى في منتخب المسند - كما في الفتح 8/ 724 - من طريق عبيد الله بن عمرو به، وأخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 384 - ومن طريقه أحمد 5/ 437 (3483)، والبخارى (4958)، والترمذى (3348)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11685)، والبيهقى في الدلائل 2/ 191، 192 - من طريق عبد الكريم به.

notes.en: Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur—as cited in the Mahmudiyya manuscript (p. 456)—to the author.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور - كما في المخطوطة المحمودية ص 456 - إلى المصنف.

notes.en: Tafsir Mujahid, p. 739. ʿAbd ibn Humayd transmitted it through Mujahid, as cited in Taghliq al-Taʿliq (4/374). Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/370) to al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 739، ومن طريقه عبد بن حميد - كما في تغليق التعليق 4/ 374 - وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 370 إلى الفريابي وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم.

notes.en: Ibn Abi Shayba (13/167, 574) and Ahmad in al-ʿIlal wa-Maʿrifat al-Rijal (1/351, no. 2196) transmitted it through Sufyan, from Abu Sinan, from ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur—as cited in the Mahmudiyya manuscript (p. 456)—to the author, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim, as a statement of ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith. Abu Sinan is Dirar ibn Murra; he narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl and ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith. See Tahdhib al-Kamal (13/307; 14/403; 16/244).
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 167، 574، وأحمد في العلل ومعرفة الرجال 1/ 351 (2196)، من طريق سفيان، عن أبي سنان، عن عبد اللَّهِ بن الحارث، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور - كما في المخطوطة المحمودية ص 456 - إلى المصنف والفريابي وابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم من قول عبد الله بن الحارث، وأبو سنان ضرار بن مرة يروى عن عبد الله بن أبى الهذيل وعبد الله بن الحارث. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 13/ 307، 14/ 403، 16/ 244.

notes.en: See al-Tibyan (10/382).
notes.ar: ينظر التبيان 10/ 382.

notes.en: Manuscript M omits it.
notes.ar: سقط من: م.
